As some may know, I've been hounding Kagura for a while. Buying and playing their games knowing they're going to be bad so I can give them a negative review. Why? Because they, more than anyone else, have a propensity to publish shovelware H-games at an alarming rate with a price point that doesn't match the quality or quantity of the game. So you may be surprised to hear that I actually enjoyed this one. I had a much longer review planned that explained the ups and downs of this game and why I eventually decided this deserved a recommend but I was roadblocked by steams character limit so I'll give the sparknotes version of it.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
It's decent. Typical rpgmaker combat. It also throws in gameplay elements from other games like claire quest, brave alchemist, etc. It has a weirdly in-depth alchemy system, a sort of boss rush mode at night with its 'terrifying enemies' as well as fishing and managing your shrine.

[h1]Story[/h1]
Also fine. What sets this apart from other games with a similar plot like Saint Emiliana or Seeds of Evil is that it's very self aware. The creator seemed to understand how cliche and ridiculous this sort of plot is and decided to lean into it.  They don't take the 'Priestess in an untenable situation must remain pure or be corrupted' premise very seriously. The game pokes fun at itself, breaks the fourth wall a couple times through books that explain plot points and game mechanics and the characters are pretty quirky and funny, making the world you inhabit endearing. 

The plot is you are sent to an island to avoid backlash from a nobleman you rejected. Once there you befriend a monster who is quickly sold off and you must cooperate with an ancient goddess to retrieve seven treasures to get her back. The game does a good job, for the most part, in allowing the player to actually make choices. Other games like this railroad you into getting raped, molested, etc. This one does that a couple times but all other interactions give you a choice and you don't appear to need to play new game+ to get the pure ending which is always a plus. That said you can almost smell the games disappointment if you choose to take the pure option with the game at multiple points just outright saying [spoiler]"It's a shame you payed all that money for the treasure key rather than just using your body. It's really unfortunate that you've chosen not to become a dedicated monster breeder ( shrine maiden ) for Noir"[/spoiler].

[h1]Art[/h1]
The art is pretty good. The side portrait of your character is hot. That said the quality of the art varies wildly from scene to scene and most scenes consist of a static image with a pair of hands or some other body part that waggles around a bit. In general I think it's pretty good but it's nothing mindblowing.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
This is one of the few games worth the asking price ( of $15 ) that Kagura has put out. The characters are charming ( some of them anyways ) the art is good and there is enough good content in the game to keep you busy for a while. The way the story was told also took me by surprise. That is to say it was funny and didn't take itself so seriously which is welcome, especially when dealing with a plot as overused as the corrupted priestess. The game does encourage you to corrupt your character and it will berate you for not doing so, sometimes subtly and sometimes directly. To get the most out of the game it's probably best not to aim for a pure play-through. At least not on your first run-through of the game. In attempting to get the 'pure ending' you miss out on a vast majority of the content and will find yourself grinding [i] a lot[/i] to make it to the end.

[spoiler]
[h1]Things I wish I knew when I started[/h1]
The chefs hat is extremely overpowered and will make getting money extremely easy. Useful for a pure play-through. Just fish to get this and then grind out the abandoned mines or the haunted shrine.

Terrifying enemies drop the most overpowered accessories in the game. Focus on trying to beat the one in the cave by the beach ( emblem gives you double attack ) and the one at the haunted/cursed shrine ( emblem heals you every time you melee an enemy ). With those two you should be able to breeze through the game relatively unscathed.
[/spoiler]

Don't forget to apply the R18 patch.

Overall, the H-scenes in this game left much to be desire.

[h1]QUICK FACTS[/h1]

Type: H-RPG
Developer: Shimobashira Workshop
Publisher: Kagura Games
Price: €12,49
Est. playtime: 15-20 hours
Censorship: yes (patch available at publisher’s website)


[h1]THE GAME[/h1]

[b]MECHANICS[/b]
Standard RPG Maker gameplay with an elaborate ruleset, including gathering & crafting, turn-based combat and multiple unlockable skill trees. You also have the possibility to upgrade your home base (a shrine) with both cosmetic and functional expansions, such as a souvenir shop that generates daily income. 

During the first part of the game, you’ll find yourself in a race against the clock: you’ll have to collect a number of artifacts within a limited timeframe in order to free a friend from captivity. This is moderately challenging, but also fully optional: failing to meet the deadline won’t affect your progression overly much.

If you play the game as it’s meant to be played, there is a bit of grinding involved, particularly in gathering resources and combat. However, Ambrosia is a pretty forgiving game: most challenges can be tackled in multiple ways and there are many items/options to be found that will make your gameplay considerably easier, if you like.

Controls: keyboard / mouse 

[b]STORY[/b]
You play as Flode, a young apprentice priestess of Leight, the light god. At the start of the game, your seniors assign you to missionary work on the remote island of Cerbes. Soon after arriving at the island, you discover that Cerbes used to be the holy place of Noir, the former goddess of the night. As the story progresses, you gradually unravel the forgotten history of Cerbes and Noir, which will put your own faith to the test.

The story is mostly lineair but has multiple endings, depending on choices you make. In addition, there are plenty of (short) optional side quests available. The overall vibe is light-hearted; even though Flode may end up in pretty nasty situations, she stays upbeat and motivated to achieve her goals throughout the game.

[b]QUALITY[/b]
When judged by gameplay alone, Ambrosia stands head and shoulders above most other games in its genre. The mechanics are interesting, diverse and balanced enough to make the game worth playing, even without lewd. The developers also did a better-than-average job on level design: dungeons are fairly varied, not too long and offer enough interesting loot and encounters to fully explore them. And while the story isn’t particularly original, Flode is a likeable character that is easy to sympathize with.

[h1]THE GOODS[/h1]

[b]SUBJECT[/b]
Nearly all lewd in Ambrosia is about Flode getting funky with various NPC’s and monsters. Scenes range from the wind accidentally lifting up your skirt to full-blown group sex, and anything in between. Most of the lewd is on the vanilla side of things; you won’t encounter all of the usual tropes for this genre. Exhibitionism on the other hand features quite prominently. Quite a few scenes start out against Flode’s will. Often, she ends up enjoying it anyway.

Keywords: [spoiler]big breasts, devices, group, fluids, forced, humiliation, incest, lesbian, monster, pregnancy, public, solo, straight, tentacles[/spoiler]

[b]CONTENT[/b]
141 scenes made out of CG’s and simple CG-based animations. Several combat animations, as well as 9 unlockable outfits. Many scenes re-use the same basic CG’s, with varying overlays (most notably the different outfits).

[b]ACCESS[/b]
You encounter lewd scenes in three ways: by performing badly during or losing certain combat encounters, by getting harassed on the street or by initiating certain quests. Almost all lewd is avoidable; it’s possible to finish the game with a (nearly) clean slate (although this can be quite challenging.)

Access to lewd is also stage-gated; you’ll need to accumulate a number of indecency points in order to progress to a higher lewdness level, after which more explicit scenes and clothing options become available.

Ambrosia doesn’t have an in-game gallery by default, but you can buy an item at a vendor that makes one available. Another purchasable item provides you with hints on how to unlock any scenes that you may have missed. After completing the game, you’ll be able to purchase a third item that unlocks any scenes you may have missed.

[b]QUALITY[/b]
The artwork is average for the genre; it’s convincing and cute, but not quite as detailed/elaborate as in some of the competing games out there. Content progression however is very good: Flode’s gradual descent into sexiness is particularly well executed, regardless of how far you decide to go.

[h1]VERRO’S VERDICT[/h1]
Ambrosia ranks right up there with Meltys Quest and Treasure Hunter Claire. The latter two perhaps have better artwork, but Ambrosia offers more in terms of gameplay. The devs have managed to hit the sweet spot between making an entertaining game, serving up a good portion of lewd and offering enough flexibility to enjoy the game the way you like. And it’s pretty cheap, too! Don’t hesitate, just buy it now.

[b][u]Gameplay? In MY H-Game!?[/u][/b]
Steam has something of a crappy RPG-Maker cash-in H-Game epidemic, and yeah, this is another one of those. Basic, mostly boring combat abounds. A pretty standard RPG Maker h-game, but there is a ton of content. If you like farming materials and grinding out levels, there's tons here for you - I'm about to quit playing at 15 hours and I honestly ended up using a save editor because I ran out of patience on getting enough XP to survive the mid-game.

[b]Content Disclaimer[/b]
The fetish themes to warn about are non-consent, mindbreak, sw, breeding, exhibition, kidnapping. If you're not comfortable with that stuff, you won't have much fun here.

[b]Story[/b]
Fairly thin, I think the writer(s) had one neat idea (not an original one, just one they liked) that they tried to spin into a game and it shows.

[b]Combat[/b]
purely early-90's turn-based jrpg style: attack, spell, defend, item, run. there's the usual "enemy is looking for an opportunity grab you!" hgame stuff, too.

[b]H Content[/b]
The content is pretty standard as these games go honestly; it has different outfits based on your character's comfort rating, loss scenes, minimal solo stuff, a small amount of b/g stuff, and mostly is group stuff with some tentacles thrown in here or there. A majority of the scenes you'll run into throughout the game are reused assets/sprites, and maybe 30 fully drawn screens are present in the h-content for the game.

[b]Unique Features[/b]
Not a ton here, but there are a good variety of locations to visit, enemies to farm for drops, an alchemist to make unique gear, a church that you can purchase decorations/upgrades for, and a surprising amount of optional and post-game content. This game also includes a NG+ feature, and a boss rush mode (sort of).

[b]Final Thoughts[/b]
Overall I'd say it's a 3.5 star game. If you like the kinds of content listed in the disclaimer about (especially mindbreak and sw), or you like grinding/farming in rpg's. If you're looking for something in a similar vein, I'd suggest Ideology in Friction or Magical Girl Celesphonia, both available from Kagura Games.

The quality varies in games like this:  From the bottom-of-the-barrel fare like [i]Paladin Lias[/i] and [i]Dark Elf[/i], to genre leaders like [i]Meltys Quest[/i].

But they all end up playing pretty much identically, with the same old tropes and the same old bland ill-conceived gameplay.

This game is exactly the same:  Same ludonarrative dissonance in throwing fights to see non-con H-scenes; same tedious second-rate RPGMaker combat; same RPGMaker assets; same poses and animations reused constantly, etc, etc.

Secretly abused by shopkeeper that you're working for while you serve customers?  Check.
Aphrodisiac flowers that you obliviously walk into and then get date-raped by the adventurer hanging around them?  Check.

This game does nothing original.  Its only unique selling point is that it features a decent amount of polish, which isn't exactly special, given that titles like [i]Meltys[/i] do broadly the same thing, and about equally as well.

[h1]The game's full of boring padding and filler that is just a time waste[/h1]

There's a crafting system which is annoying, and stingy with drops.  You're forced to enter a zone, one-shot mob after mob to get the drops, leave once you've cleared it, immediately come back to respawn the mobs, then grind grind grind some more.
And this isn't for some super epic secret item or something, just getting 3x honey from some low level bees in the very first zone takes an inordinate amount of spamming.

There's a fishing mini-game with dozens and dozens of fish to find and sell, but it doesn't really do anything interesting – just one more type of currency added to the game to get a load of simply redundant consumables.

Maybe if you wanted to raise the difficulty above the default (Normal – Story) level, then maximising your items and consumables, etc, etc might become crucial, but really *this game is not original, deep, sophisticated, interesting enough to merit that investment of your time*.

As it stands stuff like fishing, crafting, and the dull grinding just seems a totally unnecessary and redundant waste of time.  And this is emblematic of the whole game.

[b]Stuff like the in-combat h-mechanics don't seem to serve any real purpose[/b]

Compare it to [i]Karryn's Prison[/i] where the sex is a fundamental part of the combat system, and you realise just how superficial and pointless it is in this game.  Same goes for the way the game unlocks sex-passive titles that generally don't seem particularly significant or interesting; unlike [i]Karryn's Prison[/i] where they actually feel like an evolving part of the narrative.

The combat here is typical RPGmaker fare, although it is slightly streamlined with a crude skill-tree system, using Battlepoints (basically glorified XP) to purchase spells and stat boosts, etc.  But that's not enough to make it worthwhile of its own right, even if it is markedly better than stuff like [i]Fallen ~Makina and the City of Ruins~[/i].

Plenty of eroge know better than to waste your time with repetitive unnecessary combat and find ways to omit it altogether, or else sidestep it ([i]Tina: Swordswoman of the Scarlet Prison[/i] for example).  This game doesn't.

[h1]The writing's mediocre, but tolerable[/h1]

It's perfunctory, and like pretty much all games in these genres it has very little interest in building a narrative.  The characters are alright, but nothing special.  The scenes are standard.  There's no engrish or typos that I saw, so it's just "fine".  But underwhelming and not in the service of any sort of interesting story-telling.

[h1]The presentation's pretty good[/h1]

Plenty of costume changes for the main character, that are reflected in the various H-scenes she triggers going about her day.  It does a decent job of integrating all the usual gimmicks of the medium in a way that's well-realised.

If you really love these sorts of games, and don't care that they're very superficial, then this is one of the better ones – in some ways I'd say it's comparable with [i]Meltys[/i] if not outright better in a few narrow areas.

But really, there's stuff like [i]Claire's Quest[/i] that has far more going on; and there's stuff like [i]Tina: Swordswoman of the Scarlet Prison[/i] that wastes far less of your time with dull combat.

And that's before you consider all the other genres of eroge that don't have the inherent short-comings of bland JRPGs.

Let me be up front in saying that this game's fetishes are not really in my wheelhouse. The basic premise is that you're controlling a chaste, innocent priestess, and through decisions you make in game you can either keep her that way, or watch her fall into corruption through copious amounts of sex, indecency, or lost battles. The 'corruption' theme is a big part of this game's kink, and it's not one of my favorites.

That having been said, even putting aside my bias, this game is awful.

Ambrosia is a game in a similar vein to 'Treasure Hunter Claire' and 'Melty's Quest' where you control a single character throughout, with their portrait constantly hovering on the right side of the screen in whichever outfit you decide to dress them in. Flode's outfit can get torn through various overworld traps or enemy combat actions, and a sufficiently torn outfit allows enemies the chance to sexually assault them.

The place where Ambrosia falls short compared to Claire and Melty is that there's basically no interesting characters in the game whatsoever. Every one of Flode's potential partners are nameless/faceless humans, tentacle creatures, or nameless/faceless orcs. Despite the game having a great many unlockable 'scenes' there's shockingly little in the way of variety. The only thing that changes is the setting in which Flode gets assaulted by the nameless and faceless assailants, and the only other two characters in the entire game that get proper artwork don't even get scenes with Flode.

Most of these potential scenes are avoidable. Unfortunately, if you want to play this game keeping Claire focused on her mission to rescue her friend from a slaver, there's basically nothing here for you besides a very basic and sub-standard combat system, and the point where the enemies get more 'interesting' is the point where the game just flat-out stops giving you H-scenes and takes a hard turn into a more traditional RPG.

The story has the gem of an interesting idea struggling to manifest, but suffers due to the lack of any interesting characters to prop up the plot. The final villain is someone you meet briefly for less than thirty seconds and never see again until the end, and the 'good' ending doesn't even really feel like an ending instead of a return to the status quo.

In conclusion, give this game a pass. If you're still curious or 'corruption themes' are your bread and butter, try not to pay more than five dollars.

A few final notes. First, as is tradition with these sorts of games, make sure you get the free adult patch from Kagura Games website if you do want to play this despite my warnings. Second, there is an item that will unlock all of the scenes in the gallery that you can purchase after you finish the game, so don't feel like you need to go out of your way to collect them all. Most are just slight variations of the same scenes depending on Flode's level of corruption.

The game looks good, cute art, and the MC Flode is pretty likable. 

There's a lot not so great about it, though. For one, there are quite a few different CG situations but there are only a few "action" CG, and those are crudely animated with bugged z-layer issues putting strange sprites in front of others. It's hard to enjoy this way. And you can't skip any of the bad animations. You can blow through reading text a million times but not these. Which is a pity because it takes forever AND you need to rack those encounter numbers up to unlock additional buffs.

Also, this is another impossible-to-complete game without the restoration patch, which I guess it unfortunate but the gameplay itself is a little disappointing. There aren't a whole lot of tactical decisions, you versus enemy party, and you decisions are a basic attack, magic, and that's it. You can buff or anti-buff, but they don't last long enough to matter and you have to manage your health anyway. The enemies eventually outclass you where enemies are hitting you harder than you can recover and still do damage. Once that stat barrier is in place, you're basically blocked from the rest of the game until you power up. This requires a ton of grinding and, realistically, the only viable way to get the followers you need for better spells is to play Flode as a turbo-sloot the whole time. The pure route is just not viable outside of New Game +. One of the MacGuffins required to complete the game is locked behind and impossibly-priced good that you're just not going to be able to normally buy.

Also, the game is pretty locked down until you get MacGuffin 1 of 7, then it opens up. Sounds good? No, not really, because it's still stat-gated. Even with gaining stats, you're still looking at having to grind up to above Level 90 and, since the combat is so dull, you feel every encounter.

The intention might have been to just keep replaying the game to unlock the titles and skills, but with the dull combat and lack of skipping dull H scenes, I just have to say no thanks.
